processing: A bred tea plant cultivar rather than a finished tea, grown mainly for green tea, which is fixed and dried without oxidation.
harvest_season: Spring buds break in mid to late March, and one-bud-three-leaf shoots peak in mid-April. It suits machine plucking.
appearance_dry: As green tea, plump and tender with a deep, glossy green colour.
taste_profile: Green tea from it is described as fresh and brisk with a clean, distinctive aroma, helped by a balanced ratio of polyphenols to amino acids.

brewing.notes: General green tea handling; the high polyphenol content means long steeps can turn it astringent.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name. Its leaf goes into Hubei green teas, sold as the current year's harvest as is usual for the class, with spring pickings valued most.
description:
Echa No. 1 is a hybrid cultivar for green tea, grown across Hubei in places such as Xianning, Yingshan, Zhuxi, Yunxian, Xiaogan and Wuchang, and introduced into Henan and Hunan. You meet it as a plant name in a grower's notes more often than on a tea tin.

It has a half-spreading crown and branches freely. The leaves are long, oval, deep green and glossy, and the young shoots are yellow-green with moderate down. These are sturdy shoots: 100 one-bud-three-leaf shoots weigh about 91.5 g, and they stay tender for a good while.

The spring leaf's dried one-bud-two-leaf sample has about 3.0% amino acids, 29.8% polyphenols and 3.4% caffeine. Finished green tea is described as plump and deep green, with a clear bright liquor and a fresh, brisk taste.

If you see it named on a Hubei green tea, brew it as you would any spring green, and keep steeps short because of that high polyphenol level. Ask whether it is spring leaf, which is usually the most valued for the class.
history: Echa No. 1 was bred by hybridisation and spread through Hubei as a high-yield, hardy green tea plant. It received a Hubei provincial science and technology progress award. Institutions linked to its spread include the Fruit and Tea Institute of the Hubei Academy of Agricultural Sciences and Huazhong Agricultural University. The year of breeding is not stated in the accounts available.
